purpose: Apply reusable support, weight, and contact rules from page physicality.mode so stable geometry is enforced across every book.

directives: At least one clear load-bearing body part must visibly contact the named support surface.
Body weight and center of mass must read as supported by that contact; no unexplained gap beneath feet, paws, hooves, base, or root.
At least one load-bearing limb or body surface must visibly contact the ground while the action occurs.
Motion may extend other limbs away from support, but the whole creature may not accidentally become airborne.
Show one or more explicit attachment/contact points to the named support.
The support must visibly carry or anchor the creature's weight; do not place the support behind the creature without contact.
Show a readable transfer of weight between the old support and the destination surface.
At least one support contact must remain visible during the transition; never freeze the creature unsupported between surfaces.
A substantial part of the creature must remain visibly connected to the source opening, earth, tunnel, or embedding material.
Displaced material or boundary contact should identify the emergence source; do not depict an unsupported jump.
The body must visibly press against, wrap around, or remain anchored to the named support or target.
Keep contact points readable and avoid floating body segments or ambiguous merged silhouettes.
A broad portion of the amorphous body must visibly contact floor, wall, bars, steps, water, or another named support.
Stretching or flowing forms must preserve a continuous contact path rather than floating as disconnected blobs.
Airborne placement must be clearly intentional and supported by the creature's flight or magical locomotion.
Use a readable motion path or origin point so the subject does not look accidentally misplaced in midair.
The creature must visibly contact the confining geometry and at least one load-bearing support surface.
Compression and contact, not hovering, must explain the constrained pose.
Some members of the cluster must visibly contact the named feeding/support target while others may remain airborne.
Keep contact members and airborne members visually distinct enough to read the cluster's physical logic.

rule: Every physicality.mode used by an active page must resolve to exactly one reusable support family. Page support/motion text supplies the scene-specific contact detail.
